<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is sourced only at the top level. All variable assignments, array definitions, and the `for`/`eval` block that sets `source_*=` variables are standard AUR packaging idioms; they assign URLs to source arrays without performing any network access or code execution. The `eval` string contains only variable expansions of previously defined safe variables (_pkgname, _arch, pkgver) and does not invoke any external commands. No command substitution, `curl`, `wget`, `base64`, `eval` of decoded blobs, or data exfiltration occurs at the top level. The `sha256sums` arrays contain 'SKIP' entries, but as noted, missing checksums are not evaluated during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. The `verify()` and `package()` functions are defined later and are not executed at this stage. Consequently, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` poses no risk of executing malicious code.
</details>
